prompts.text: Please use keywords or phrases, separated by commas, to identify your research interests more specifically. Do not use tabs or add lines by hitting the enter key. There is a limit of 500 characters.

List you research experience chronologically, starting with the most recent, and including your anticipated experience for the remainder of this academic year. For each experience, please provide clear information about the time commitment. (For instance, if you worked continuously in one lab for a year, putting in full time hours during the summer, and part time hours during the school year, you might state: “full time (about 50 hours a week) from mid May until the end of August, continuing part time (about 10 hours a week) from September to April”. Note that if you worked two summers in the same lab, but did not work in that lab at all during the school year, these should be listed as two separate research experiences.) For each experience, indicate whether your mentor will provide a letter of recommendation. If you do not select a letter from an individual with whom you had an extensive research experience, please provide an explanation in the comments section.

Prompt 2 joined from the sentence plus its parenthetical '(MSTP will consider information provided here as well as your AMCAS Personal Comments):'; prompt 5 joined from 2 quoted pieces; prompt 6 joined from 2 pieces (post labels it as 'in the coursework section under social studies/humanities'); prompt 4 marked '(optional)'. No 2026-2027 MSTP wording found: 2026-2027 thread pages 1-3 checked earlier; UW MSTP how-to-apply (2026-2027 timeline) and FAQ pages describe the 'UW MSTP Secondary Application' ($35, Dec 15 deadline) but list no prompts. FAQ says UW MSTP and UW Medical School have separate admissions processes; non-WWAMI applicants must choose Regular MD or MD/PhD in AMCAS, and a complete MSTP application = AMCAS + UW MSTP secondary + fee + letters (basis for md_secondary 'instead'; WWAMI residents can be considered for both). SDN schools-database lists 3 similar MSTP prompts for 2020-2021 only (older wording: 'How did you learn about...', 'Please use this opportunity...'), not used.

prompts.text: Indicate the area(s) of research in which you are interested.
Please use this space to supplement your AMCAS Personal Comments. (MSTP will consider information provided here as well as your AMCAS Personal Comments):
How did you find out about the University of Washington's Medical Scientist Training Program?
Use this opportunity to provide any autobiographical information which you feel would be helpful for the MSTP office.
If you are not currently enrolled in coursework (nor planning to be enrolled throughout the application process), please describe your activities in this period.
Describe your competency by explaining how you have explored and come to understand issues in the social sciences and humanities as they relate to the practice of medicine.

school: Weill Cornell Medicine (NY)
source_note: From SDN 2025-2026 Weill Cornell thread page 1, post #10 (deleted1220651, Jun 30 2025): the MD-PhD secondary matches the MD one except 'Question 1 is instead please write a brief statement giving your reasons for applying to the Tri-Institutional MD-PhD Program.' plus one added question; 'Both are 1525 characters'. Prompt text recorded exactly as the poster typed it (lowercase 'please'; the poster's lead-in 'Question 1 is instead' omitted). Left out: the added faculty-name list question ('Please list the names of any Tri-Institutional faculty members with whom you would like to do research...' - poster says no reasons needed, names suffice; a bare name list). Since MD-PhD applicants answer the rest of the MD secondary, md_secondary set 'also' (Q1 is replaced). No 2026-2027 wording found: 2026-2027 thread is single-page (checked earlier); Tri-I MD-PhD admissions FAQ (mdphd.weill.cornell.edu) says only that applicants complete 'Tri-I's Secondary Application' after AMCAS verification, no prompts. ProspectiveDoctor lists the faculty-names question (200 words) only for 2017-2018/2018-2019.

prompts.text: please write a brief statement giving your reasons for applying to the Tri-Institutional MD-PhD Program.

school: Yale School of Medicine (CT)
source_note: From SDN 2025-2026 Yale thread page 1, post #21 (imsogonnagetrejected, Jul 17 2025), headed 'MD PhD Essay'; joined from the lead-in plus 3 bullet lines, quoted in consecutive pieces (post ends 'career goals..' - duplicate period dropped). Post #9 (deleted1220651, Jul 1 2025) corroborates: the MD/PhD secondary has the same questions as the MD version plus one additional statement, opening 'Write a statement concerning your reasons for wishing to undertake the combined MD/PhD program' (wording differs slightly from #21 - 'MD/PhD' vs 'MD PhD', no word count; #9 not fully quotable). Posts #1 (Apr 17 2025) and #4 (Jun 30 2025) also carry the instruction 'MD/PhD applicants: Please answer question 2 as it pertains to your proposed PhD research.' (shared Essay 2, not recorded; same as 2026-2027 per prior note). No 2026-2027 MD/PhD-only wording found: 2026-2027 thread single page (checked earlier, post #15 question unanswered). Yale MD-PhD application process page (medicine.yale.edu/mdphd/prospective/applicationprocess, updated Mar 10 2026) says MD-PhD applicants complete the Yale Secondary Application (confirms md_secondary 'also'); it lists no essay prompts, and describes only (not recorded) a 500-1,000 word 'personal statement of academic purpose' for non-traditional PhD programs (Anthropology, History of Science & Medicine, Philosophy, Religious Studies, Sociology), due Oct 15. Note: the 2026-2027 SDN thread (post #6) says MD/PhD applicants answer regular question 2 with their PhD research in mind, so this 2025-2026 prompt may have been retired.

prompts.text: Write a statement (approximately 500 words) concerning: Your reasons for wishing to undertake the combined MD PhD program, rather than the MD program alone. The specific PhD program that you propose to follow at Yale. The strengths of that Yale graduate program and its faculty as they relate to your career goals.
